mainTopic: Traveling into ארץ העמים inside a box, and רב חסדא on when a מצורע נזיר must restart his count
overview: The גמרא tries to show that the question of whether the רבנן's decree on ארץ העמים is about its air or its earth is already a dispute of תנאים. רבי says a person who enters ארץ העמים inside a chest, box, or cabinet is impure, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he is pure. The first suggestion is that both hold the decree is about the earth, and they argue over whether a moving tent (אהל זרוק) counts as a tent. A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds a moving tent is not a tent, so that explanation falls. Instead, both may hold the decree is about the air, and they argue whether the רבנן decreed even for a rare case; a ברייתא backs this up. A second explanation is that they argue only over the worry that he will put his head and most of his body outside the box, and another ברייתא supports that. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that a נזיר who became a מצורע 'starts and counts' again. רב חסדא limits this to a short נזירות. רב שרביא begins challenging him from the משנה, and his challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Linking the air-or-earth question to an earlier dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the question of air or earth is the same as the dispute between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה about someone who enters ארץ העמים inside a closed container.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like a dispute of תנאים. Someone enters ארץ העמים inside a chest, a box, or a cabinet. רבי says he is impure, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he is pure. Isn't it that רבי holds the decree is about the air, and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds it is about the earth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that our question, whether the decree on ארץ העמים is about its air or its earth, was already argued by two תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the decree is about the air, a person inside a box is still in the land's air, so he is impure. If the decree is about the earth, the box keeps him apart from the ground, so he stays pure. That would neatly explain why רבי says impure and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says pure.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like a dispute of תנאים
Lands outside ארץ ישראל, which the רבנן declared impure
A chest, a box, and a cabinet: large closed containers a person can ride inside
The air or airspace
The clod, meaning the earth or soil
Isn't it that…? (opens a suggested reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' with no name after it means רבי יהודה הנשיא. He is a different person from רבי יהודה, the father of רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute between תנאים:
One who enters the land of the nations
in a chest, a box, or a cabinet,
Rabbi deems him impure,
and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda deems him pure.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו: רַבִּי סָבַר מִשּׁוּם אַוֵּירָא,
phrases.english: Is it not that Rabbi holds the decree is because of the air,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר מִשּׁוּם גּוּשָּׁא?
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda holds it is because of the earth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the earlier question of air versus earth to a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: That the question of air versus earth is already a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about entering ארץ העמים in a שידה, תיבה, or מגדל

steps.title: Both may hold it is the earth; the dispute is about a moving tent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: both may agree the decree is about the earth. They argue only over whether a moving container counts as a tent (אהל) that blocks טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone holds the decree is because of the earth. One holds that a moving tent is called a tent, and the other holds it is not called a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the link it just suggested and offers another way to explain the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both hold the decree is about the earth, the question becomes whether a box that is moving can act as a tent between the person and the ground. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה would say a moving tent counts, so the person is pure. רבי would say it does not count, so the person is impure.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees
A thrown or moving tent: something that covers only while it is in motion
It is called a tent and has the law of a tent
One master holds…

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees it is because of the earth.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: אֹהֶל זָרוּק — שְׁמֵיהּ אֹהֶל,
phrases.english: One master holds: a moving tent is called a tent,
phrases.notes: This first 'master' is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who says the person is pure.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: it is not called a tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed link and moves the dispute onto the question of אהל זרוק.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Denies that the ברייתא shows a dispute about air versus earth
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be explained another way, as a question of whether a moving tent counts as a tent

steps.title: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה himself holds a moving tent is not a tent
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה ruling that a box thrown over a corpse is impure. This shows he does not treat a moving tent as a tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: if a box full of utensils is thrown over a corpse in a tent, it is impure. If it was set down, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the explanation from the last step using a ruling that comes from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ruling, the box protects its contents only when it rests in place, not while it flies over the corpse. So for רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, a moving tent is not a tent. That is the opposite of what the last step said in his name.

keyTerms.meaning: He threw it
Placed down, resting in place

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
A box that is full of utensils,

phrases.aramaic: וּזְרָקָהּ עַל פְּנֵי הַמֵּת בְּאֹהֶל — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: and he threw it over a corpse in a tent: it is impure,
and if it was placed down, it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds אהל זרוק שמיה אהל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He rules that a thrown box does not protect what is inside it. So in his view a moving tent is not a tent.

steps.title: Both hold it is the air; they argue whether the decree covers a rare case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its explanation. Both hold the decree is about the air. They argue only over whether the רבנן made their decree for something that rarely happens, like travelling inside a box.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, everyone holds the decree is because of the air. One holds that since this is not common, the רבנן did not make the decree for it. The other holds that even though it is not common, the רבנן did make the decree for it.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the last explanation failed, the גמרא gives a new explanation: both sides agree the decree is about the air, so their dispute does not depend on the air-or-earth question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everyone holds the decree is about the air, then by plain logic the person in the box should be impure. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה still says pure because riding into the land inside a box is rare, and the רבנן did not decree about rare cases. רבי says the רבנן decreed even about this rare case. So the ברייתא does not prove anything about air versus earth.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (drops the last explanation and gives a new one)
It is not common, it rarely happens
The רבנן made a decree
Even though

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to tie the air-or-earth question to the dispute of רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה fails. In this answer, both hold the decree is about the air, and they argue only whether the רבנן decreed even for a rare case, like entering inside a box. Step 6 gives a second explanation.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common idea: the רבנן sometimes do not extend a decree to unusual cases, and תנאים can argue about whether they did.

phrases.english: Rather, everyone agrees it is because of the air,
and one master holds: since it is not common,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who rules the person pure.

phrases.english: the Rabbis did not decree about it,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא שְׁכִיחָא —
phrases.english: and the other master holds: even though it is not common,
the Rabbis did decree about it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3 by giving a new explanation of the dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New explanation of what the dispute between תנאים is about
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about air versus earth, or else about אהל זרוק
steps.terutzMaskana: Both hold the decree is about the air. They argue whether the רבנן decreed for a case that is לא שכיחא.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that common vehicles were included in the decree but rare containers were not
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that someone entering ארץ העמים in a chest, box, or cabinet is pure, but someone in a wagon, boat, or raft is impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught: Someone who enters ארץ העמים in a chest, a box, or a cabinet is pure. Someone in a wagon, a boat, or a raft is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the answer from Step 4: the רבנן did not make their decree for rare situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People travel in wagons, boats, and rafts all the time, so the decree covers them and the traveller is impure. Hardly anyone travels inside a chest or a box, so the רבנן never decreed on that, and the traveller stays pure. This fits רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's view as Step 4 explained it.

keyTerms.meaning: A chest, a box, and a cabinet: closed containers that people rarely travel in
A wagon
A raft or small boat
Pure / impure

phrases.english: And it is taught: One who enters the land of the nations
phrases.notes: Here 'and it is taught' brings support for the last answer, not a challenge.

phrases.english: in a chest, a box, or a cabinet is pure;
in a wagon, a boat, or a raft, he is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the explanation in Step 4 that the argument is about whether the רבנן decreed for rare cases.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the רבנן did not apply the decree to rare ways of travel such as inside a box.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that separates rare containers (pure) from common vehicles (impure).

steps.title: Another explanation: they argue over whether he might stick his head out
steps.stepSummary: Another way to read it: both agree the person is protected. They argue only over the worry that he might put his head and most of his body outside the container.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: here they argue over the worry that he might put his head and most of his body out there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different way to understand the argument between רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, both agree the decree is about the earth and that a moving tent counts as a tent, so the container should protect him. The only question is whether we fear he will lean his head and most of his body outside into ארץ העמים. רבי worries about this and calls him impure. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה does not.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: this introduces another possible answer
His head and most of his body
They argue

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new challenge. It is simply a second way to explain the same argument, alongside the explanation from Step 4.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: here

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא יוֹצִיא רֹאשׁוֹ וְרוּבּוֹ לְשָׁם פְּלִיגִי.
phrases.english: they argue over the worry that he may put his head and most of his body out there.
phrases.notes: 'There' means outside the container, into ארץ העמים itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second explanation next to Step 4 for what רבי and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argue about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the argument to a different point: a practical worry, not the nature of the decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument depends on how the decree was defined, either air versus earth or rare cases.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue only over whether we worry that he will put his head and most of his body outside the container.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה makes him impure only if he actually leans out
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: the person in the container is pure unless he actually puts his head or most of his body outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is taught: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says, someone who enters ארץ העמים in a chest, a box, or a cabinet is pure, until he puts his head or most of his body out there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support the second explanation from Step 6.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה makes him impure only when he actually puts his head or most of his body outside. So the question is about leaning out, as Step 6 said. רבי, who calls him impure even before that, must be worried that he will lean out.

keyTerms.meaning: Until he puts out, meaning only when he actually does it
His head or most of his body

steps.whatToRemember: There are two explanations of the argument about travelling in a box: (1) whether the רבנן decreed for rare cases, and (2) whether we worry that he will lean his head and most of his body out. Each one has a supporting ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And it is taught: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
One who enters the land of the nations
in a chest, a box, or a cabinet is pure,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיּוֹצִיא לְשָׁם רֹאשׁוֹ אוֹ רוּבּוֹ.
phrases.english: until he puts his head or most of his body out there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second explanation given in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the argument turns on the worry that he will put his head and most of his body outside.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה makes him impure only once he actually leans out.

steps.title: רב חסדא limits starting the count again to a short נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'he starts and counts.' רב חסדא says this applies only to a short נזירות. In a long נזירות, those days also count for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And he starts and counts.' רב חסדא said: They taught this only about a short נזירות. But in a long נזירות, those days also count toward it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to a new topic. It quotes the משנה's rule that a נזיר who became a מצורע starts counting again, and brings רב חסדא's limit on that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that a נזיר who becomes a מצורע starts counting his נזירות again after he becomes pure. רב חסדא says this is true only for a short נזירות. In a long נזירות, the days are not lost; they still count toward his total.

keyTerms.meaning: He starts and counts: he begins counting his days again
They taught this only about: this phrase limits a rule
A short נזירות
A long נזירות
They count toward it for him

phrases.english: "And he starts and counts."
phrases.notes: These are the משנה's words about a נזיר during the days he is a מצורע and similar cases.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
They taught this only about a short naziriteship.
But in a long naziriteship,
they also count toward it for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It leaves the ארץ העמים discussion and returns to a phrase in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that a מצורע נזיר starts counting again applies only to a short נזירות. In a long נזירות, those days still count toward his total.

steps.title: רב שרביא challenges רב חסדא from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב שרביא quotes the משנה: 'he starts counting immediately and does not cancel the earlier days.' He asks what case this is. It cannot be a short נזירות, since the נזיר needs time for his hair to grow back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שרביא raised an objection: The משנה says, 'He starts counting right away, and he does not cancel the earlier days because of them.' What case is this talking about? If you say it is a short נזירות, that cannot be right, because he needs time for his hair to grow!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שרביא begins an attack on רב חסדא's rule from step 8 by quoting another line of the משנה. He rules out one possible reading, and the גמרא is setting up the next part of his challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the earlier days are not cancelled, so he simply continues counting. In a short נזירות, though, a מצורע who shaved would have to wait for his hair to grow back, so you could not say he just continues. That pushes the משנה toward a long נזירות, which seems to clash with how רב חסדא read the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Cancels the earlier days of נזירות that were already counted
A short נזירות, the standard thirty days
Hair growth, which a נזירות needs to have
'If you say...', which brings up a possible reading so the גמרא can test it

steps.confusionAlert: This is not yet the full objection. Here רב שרביא only rules out the short נזירות, and the rest of his argument comes next.

phrases.english: Rav Sherevya raises an objection:
He starts and counts immediately,
phrases.notes: This is quoted from our משנה, about the נזיר who was a מצורע.

phrases.english: and he does not cancel the earlier days because of them.
What case is this about?
If you say it is about a short נזירות,
he needs hair growth!
phrases.notes: He shaved because of his צרעת, so his hair has to grow back before his נזירות can be finished.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's split between short and long נזירות from step 8, using another clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that the משנה's 'he starts and counts' applies only to a short נזירות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's line 'he does not cancel the earlier days' cannot fit a short נזירות, because a מצורע who shaved needs time for his hair to regrow. So the line must be about a long נזירות, which seems to work against רב חסדא's reading.
